'''Vasilis M. Fthenakis''' is a [[Greek Americans|Greek American]] [[chemical engineer]], environmental scientist, author and academic. He is an adjunct professor, and founding director of the center for [[Life-cycle assessment|Life Cycle Analysis]] at [[Columbia University]].<ref name=aaa>{{cite web|url=https://www.eee.columbia.edu/faculty/vasilis-fthenakis|title=Columbia University–Vasilis Fthenakis|date=13 June 2017 }}</ref><ref name=ccc>{{cite web|url=http://www.clca.columbia.edu/people.html|title=CLCA–People}}</ref>

Fthenakis is most known for his research on the environmental [[sustainability]] of [[Photovoltaics|photovoltaic]] energy technologies and for demonstrating the feasibility of [[solar energy]] as a solution to meet US energy demands while addressing climate challenges.<ref name=ggg>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=JAaO3voAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Google Scholar–Vasilis Fthenakis}}</ref> His publications comprise journal articles and books including ''Electricity from Sunlight: Photovoltaics Systems Integration and Sustainability'' and ''Onshore and Offshore Wind Energy: Evolution, Grid Integration and Impact''. He has received awards such as a Certificate of Appreciation from the [[United States Department of Energy|US Department of Energy]] in 2006,<ref name=doe>{{cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=110502|title=Department of Energy Honors Brookhaven Lab Scientist Vasilis Fthenakis for Photovoltaic Environmental Research}}</ref> the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]'s Certificate of Recognition in 2015, the 2018 IEEE William Cherry Award,<ref name=wca>{{cite web|url=https://ieee-pvsc.org/PVSC49/awards-cherry.php|title=William R. Cherry Award}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vasilis Fthenakis Receives IEEE's William R. Cherry Award|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=112951}}</ref> and the 2022 Karl Böer Solar Energy Medal of Merit from the [[International Solar Energy Society]].<ref name=kbs>{{cite web|url=https://www.udel.edu/udaily/2022/april/karl-boer-medal-photovoltaics-sustainable-energy-vasilis-fthenakis-anke-weidenkaff/#:~:text=Vasilis%20Fthenakis%2C%20a%20pioneer%20in,comes%20with%20a%20%24100%2C000%20prize.|title=Winners of 2022 Böer awards announced}}</ref>

Fthenakis is an elected Fellow of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]], the International Energy Foundation, and the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37267728500|title=IEEE–Vasilis Fthenakis}}</ref> Additionally, he has served as Editor-in-Chief of ''Green Energy and Sustainability'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pivotscipub.com/ges/editorial_board|title=Green Energy and Sustainability–Editorial Board}}</ref> Section Editor-in-Chief of ''[[Energies (journal)|Energies]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/energies/history|title=Energies–Journal History}}</ref> and associate editor for ''Progress in Energy''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://publishingsupport.iopscience.iop.org/journals/progress-in-energy/editorial-board/|title=Progress in Energy–Editorial Board}}</ref>

==Education and early career==
Fthenakis earned a diploma in [[chemistry]] from the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|University of Athens]] in 1975 while working as a [[chemist]] at ChemiResearch in [[Greece]] from 1974 to 1976. He then completed an MS in [[Chemical Engineering]] at Columbia University in 1978 and held research roles at Columbia's Catalysis Laboratory and Fossil Energy Laboratory. In 1980, he joined Brookhaven National Laboratory, working as a research engineer and senior scientist across departments focused on [[sustainable energy]] and [[environmental science]]s. He received a PhD in [[fluid dynamics]] and [[atmospheric science]] from [[New York University]] in 1991, with a focus on toxic gas release modeling and mitigation using water spray systems.<ref name=aaa/>

==Career==
Fthenakis continued his academic and research career at Columbia University, serving as an adjunct associate professor of earth and environmental engineering from 1995 to 2000, and has been an adjunct professor since 2006. In 2006, he became a senior research scientist and founded the Center for Life Cycle Analysis (CLCA), where he continues to serve as director. He also co-founded the Global Clean Water Desalination Alliance (GCWDA), where he served on the board of directors, leading efforts to integrate solar energy systems with [[desalination]] technologies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jppb51.wixsite.com/gcwdalliance/governance|title=GCWDA Board}}</ref> Concurrently, at Brookhaven National Laboratory, he served in various roles from 1980 to 2016 and has been a distinguished scientist emeritus since 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=212481|title=Vasilis Fthenakis Named Senior Scientist Emeritus}}</ref> From 2002 to 2016, he led the National Photovoltaic Environmental Research Center and has coordinated international collaborations on life cycle assessment (LCA) under the direction of the US Department of Energy and the [[International Energy Agency]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://energy.gov/eere/solar/project-profile-columbia-university-solar-desalination|title=Project Profile: Columbia University (Solar Desalination)}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Fthenakis has led collaborations on [[silane]] safety and lead-free [[solder]] technologies, conducted foundational life-cycle studies on [[Thin-film solar cell|thin-film photovoltaics]] and PV recycling, and anticipated regulatory trends concerning [[lead]] and [[cadmium]], supporting industry adaptation.<ref name=aaa/><ref name=ggg/> In later years, the scope of his research expanded to topics at the energy-water-environment nexus and he led applied research on [[Solar desalination|solar-powered water desalination]] with applications in the United States<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engineering.columbia.edu/about/news/vasilis-fthenakis-wins-2022-boer-solar-energy-medal-merit|title=Vasilis Fthenakis Wins the 2022 Böer Solar Energy Medal of Merit|date=15 May 2024 }}</ref> and [[Chile]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://globalcenters.columbia.edu/news/solar-expert-leads-energy-discussion|title=Solar Expert Leads Energy Discussion}}</ref>

In 2004, Fthenakis began studying life cycle analysis (LCA) to address what he identified as an unbalanced portrayal of photovoltaics' environmental impacts and started an international collaboration to update LCA studies on photovoltaics. He established an ad-hoc committee and organized scoping meetings with researchers from institutions such as the [[Utrecht University|University of Utrecht]], the [[Energy Research Centre of the Netherlands|Energy Research Center of the Netherlands]], [[Chalmers University of Technology|Chalmers University]], the [[University of Stuttgart]], [[University of Siena|Siena University]], and Ambient Italia to assess the LCA needs of the photovoltaic industry.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/es071763q|title=Emissions from Photovoltaic Life Cycles|date=2008 |doi=10.1021/es071763q |last1=Fthenakis |first1=Vasilis M. |last2=Kim |first2=Hyung Chul |last3=Alsema |first3=Erik |journal=Environmental Science & Technology |volume=42 |issue=6 |pages=2168–2174 |pmid=18409654 |bibcode=2008EnST...42.2168F |hdl=1874/32964 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2008.09.017|title=Land use and electricity generation: A life-cycle analysis|date=2009 |doi=10.1016/j.rser.2008.09.017 |last1=Fthenakis |first1=Vasilis |last2=Kim |first2=Hyung Chul |journal=Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews |volume=13 |issue=6–7 |pages=1465–1474 |bibcode=2009RSERv..13.1465F |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Through related research, Fthenakis has developed and advocated for a proactive, long-term environmental strategy for photovoltaics, including recycling processes for end-of-life photovoltaic modules. In 1999, he organized a workshop to promote lead-free solder technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clca.columbia.edu/Lead-free_Technology_Transfer_1999.pdf|title=Lead-free Solder Technology Transfer from ASE Americas}}</ref> From 2002 to 2005, he established a laboratory focused on recycling spent photovoltaic modules and manufacturing scrap, employing hydrometallurgical separation technologies and resulting in a patented method for separating [[copper]], [[cadmium]], and [[tellurium]], with applications in [[Cadmium telluride|cadmium telluride (CdTe)]] and [[Copper indium gallium selenide|copper indium gallium selenide (CIGS)]] technologies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US7731920B2/en|title=System and method for separating tellurium from cadmium waste}}</ref> He also conducted studies on optimizing the collection of end-of-life photovoltaics to reduce recycling costs.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0301-4215(00)00091-4|title=End-of-life management and recycling of PV modules|date=2000 |doi=10.1016/S0301-4215(00)00091-4 |last1=Fthenakis |first1=Vasilis M. |journal=Energy Policy |volume=28 |issue=14 |pages=1051–1058 |bibcode=2000EnPol..28.1051F |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Recognizing the environmental concerns surrounding the growth of the CdTe and CIGS markets, he designed experiments simulating fire effects on photovoltaics using techniques such as NSLS-x ray diffraction analysis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=fcb89e8d6bc1e2b5bcade5ae2d52f363d8f5dd30|title=Experimental investigation of emissions and redistribution of elements in CdTe PV modules during fires}}</ref> In 2005, he led a European Union workshop, organized with the [[Joint Research Centre|Joint Research Center]] and the [[Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection|German Ministry of the Environment]], facilitating a US company's establishment of a manufacturing facility in [[Germany]]. In 2007, he launched and led a five-year International Energy Agency (IEA) Photovoltaic Environmental Health and Safety Task (Task 12), serving as the US Operating Agent until 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iea-pvps.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Task_12_-_Methodology_Guidelines_on_Life_Cycle_Assessment_of_Photovoltaic_Electricity_3rd_Edition.pdf|title=Methodology Guidelines on Life Cycle–Assessment of Photovoltaic Electricity }}</ref>

Over the years, Fthenakis’ research has been highlighted by news outlets, including ''[[The New York Times]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/26/science/26obsola.html|title=Photovoltaic Cells Are Still Very Green, Comparative Test Shows|website=[[The New York Times]] }}</ref> ''[[Science News]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencenews.org/article/greener-green-energy-todays-solar-cells-give-more-they-take|title=Greener Green Energy: Today's solar cells give more than they take|date=27 February 2008 }}</ref> ''[[Environmental Science & Technology]]'', ''[[IEEE Spectrum]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/space-based-solar-power-2668897407|title=Space-Based Solar Power Gets Practical}}</ref> ''[[Scientific American]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/solar-cells-prove-cleaner-way-to-produce-power/|title=Dark Side of Solar Cells Brightens|website=[[Scientific American]] }}</ref> ''[[Der Spiegel|Spiegel]]'', and ''[[NRC (newspaper)|NRC Handelsblad]]''.

==Publications==
Fthenakis' research on photovoltaics and the environment has led to approximately 300 journal and conference papers, contributing to over 450 publications on energy and environmental topics. As of November 15, 2024, his publications have been cited 18,464 times and his h-index is 66.<ref name=ggg/> In 2007, he co-authored the ''Grand Plan for Solar Energy'' with Ken Zweibel and James Mason, a study demonstrating the feasibility of solar energy to meet most of the US electricity needs; this was the prelude of the detailed [[SunShot Initiative|SunShot]] Solar Vision studies.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1038/scientificamerican0108-64|title=A Solar Grand Plan|date=2008 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0108-64 |last1=Zweibel |first1=Ken |last2=Mason |first2=James |last3=Fthenakis |first3=Vasilis |journal=Scientific American |volume=298 |issue=1 |pages=64–73 |pmid=18225697 |bibcode=2008SciAm.298a..64Z |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Earlier, in 1993, he published his first book, ''Prevention and Control of Accidental Releases of Hazardous Gases'', which was used by the chemical and oil refinery industries as a primer on the prevention of industrial disasters. His publications have also focused on electricity generation through renewable energy sources such as wind and solar.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/6e078f8aca40f4b4be90e0149675f5f6/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=47267|title=Prevention and Control of Accidental Releases of Hazardous Gases|website=[[ProQuest]] }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fthenakis is the son of Menelaos Fthenakis and Antonia Korkidis-Fthenakis, who died in the sinking of the [[SS Heraklion|SS ''Heraklion'']] in Greece when he was 14 years old.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news247.gr/magazine/past/i-pragmatiki-istoria-gia-to-navagio-tis-falkoneras-sto-opoio-den-sothikan-ginaikes-kai-paidia/|title=Η Πραγματικη Ιστορια Για Το Ναυαγιο Τησ Φαλκονερασ Στο Οποιο Δεν Σωθηκαν Γυναικεσ Και Παιδια|date=29 October 2023 }}</ref> He is married to Christina Georgakopoulos and has two children and two grandchildren.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tbrnewsmedia.com/bnls-fthenakis-helps-warm-chile-to-solar-plan/|title=BNL's Fthenakis helps warm Chile to solar plan|date=6 February 2015 }}</ref>
